terms.meaning: A label that says what shape a piece of data must have.
A value whose contents the checker does not inspect, so errors show up later.
A date written as year, month, day, such as 2026-11-11.
A choice that hides items which do not match it.

sections.name: File setup, TimeframeMode, EventTypeFilter
sections.title: Imports, time ranges and filters
sections.what: Brings in icons, the store, shared pieces, editing pop-ups and the item types. Names the time range choices (daily, monthly, yearly) and the item type filter choices.
sections.why: Likely reason: the list can be narrowed by time range and item type, so the valid choices are named once.
sections.watch_out: A new filter choice must be added here and also handled in the code that filters, or it will not work.

sections.name: UnifiedEvent
sections.title: Shared agenda item shape
sections.what: Defines one common shape for every kind of agenda entry, with a title, type, date, optional time and subtitle, optional label and colour style, and the original source item.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets tasks, hackathons, internships, assignments, goals and time blocks sit in one list. Reason for keeping the original item is not stated.
sections.watch_out: The original source item is untyped, so its fields are not checked and mistakes may only appear when the app runs.

sections.name: UpcomingEventsView (part 1)
sections.title: Gather items and set up filters
sections.what: Starts the screen and reads tasks, hackathons, and related lists from the store. Turns each task and hackathon that has a date into one shared item, and keeps the current timeframe, type filter, search text, and which edit window is open.
sections.why: Likely reason: one combined list lets a single screen show every kind of deadline together. Reason for using today's date from UTC is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Today's date comes from UTC, so near midnight a user in a time zone behind UTC may see the wrong day's items as today.

sections.name: UpcomingEventsView (part 2)
sections.title: Add internships, assignments, and goals
sections.what: Adds internships, assignments, and goals to the shared list, each using its most relevant date. Items with no date are skipped, so they do not appear in any timeframe.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code, though each source follows the same pattern as the others.
sections.watch_out: Internships use the deadline first and then the application date, while hackathons check three date fields, so similar items can land on different days.

sections.name: UpcomingEventsView (part 3)
sections.title: Add timeblocks and sort by date
sections.what: Adds calendar time blocks to the list with their time range, then sorts the full list so the earliest date comes first.
sections.why: Likely reason: sorting by date makes upcoming items read from top to bottom.
sections.watch_out: Sorting compares dates as plain text, so any date stored in a different format will sort in the wrong place.

sections.name: UpcomingEventsView: switch
sections.title: Coloured label for each item type
sections.what: Shows a coloured label with a small icon for each item type, such as Task, Hackathon, Internship, Assignment, Goal Target, or Timeblock. This is done by the renderItemBadge function.
sections.why: Likely reason: colour and icon let the user recognise the type of each item at a glance.
sections.watch_out: The switch has no fallback case, so a new item type added elsewhere would show no label at all.

sections.name: UpcomingEventsView (part 5)
sections.title: Timeframe, search, and filter controls
sections.what: Draws the top panel with Daily, Monthly, and Yearly buttons, a search box, and a row of type filter buttons. Changing any of these changes which items are listed.
sections.why: Likely reason: filters let the user narrow a long list without leaving the screen.
sections.watch_out: The search also matches the date text, so typing a year or month can match many items you did not intend.

sections.name: UpcomingEventsView (part 6)
sections.title: Item list and empty message
sections.what: Shows how many items match the current view, then either an empty message suggesting a wider view or a clickable row for each item with its title, subtitle, date, and time.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The empty message suggests users should widen the filters when nothing shows.
sections.watch_out: Each row passes the original record to its editor, so a change to the shape of those records could break the edit windows.

sections.name: UpcomingEventsView (part 7)
sections.title: Edit windows for tasks, hackathons, and internships
sections.what: Opens the matching edit window for a task, hackathon, or internship when its row is clicked. Each window closes by clearing its selected item.
sections.why: Likely reason: editing from this list lets the user change an item without leaving the screen.
sections.watch_out: Each window is shown only while its selected item is set, so forgetting to clear that state would leave the window stuck open.

sections.name: UpcomingEventsView (part 8)
sections.title: Edit windows for assignments and goals
sections.what: Opens the edit window for an assignment or goal when its row is clicked, and closes it the same way as the others.
sections.why: Same likely reason as the other edit windows. Reason for splitting these into separate sections is not stated.
sections.watch_out: New item types need their own entry in the click handler, or clicking them will do nothing.

summary: Builds one combined agenda from several kinds of items, with filters. Only two of ten sections were provided, so most of its behavior is unclear here.
purpose: Gives the user a single list of upcoming items, which the visible code suggests but does not fully show.
why: Likely reason: one combined list is easier to scan than separate screens for each kind of item. The full reason is only partly visible.
how: The top of the file names the time range choices (daily, monthly, yearly) and the item type filters. It also defines one shared shape that every item is converted into so they can be listed together. The steps that do the conversion and the drawing are in sections not provided.
inputs: Tasks, hackathons, internships, assignments and goals from the store, plus time blocks from the calendar, as implied by the imports and the shared shape. Search and filter choices, as suggested by the imported icons.
outputs: Not visible in the provided sections. The shared shape describes one agenda entry with a title, type, date, optional time and subtitle, an optional label, and the original source item.
risks: The original source item is stored as an untyped value, so mistakes in it are not caught before the app runs. Dates must be written as year, month, day text or filtering may fail. Most of the file was not provided, so other risks cannot be judged.
debug: If an item shows the wrong date, check how it is converted into the shared shape. If a filter does nothing, the matching code is in sections not provided. If an editing pop-up does not open, check its import and the state that controls it.
